analysis.title: Monday Kick-off
key_insights: Last week was a rotation rather than a broad sell-off. Money moved out of AI-related stocks into cyclical sectors and select large-cap tech. The S&P 500 closed +1.4% on the week after four weekly losses, and the Nasdaq 100 rose 2.1%.
Nvidia headlines dominated after the report that Huang resigned as CEO amid China spy allegations. Nvidia reports Q3 earnings Tuesday 17 November.

European equities outperformed on lower crude (back toward USD 90-91 a barrel on hopes of a US-Iran breakthrough), solid earnings and bank M&A. The STOXX Europe 600 set a new all-time high, passing its August high on Wednesday.

US yields rebounded after a hotter CPI print (+0.4% headline, +0.3% core m/m) and hawkish comments from Fed Governor Waller. The 10-year yield briefly moved back above 5%. Markets priced a 96% probability of a December hike and 55 bp of cumulative hikes through year-end 2027.

Waller backed a 25 bp hike in December and said 50 bp could be warranted if October core CPI stays at or above 0.3% m/m. He argued policy may be less restrictive than thought and that the Fed may need to reverse at least last year's three insurance cuts.
Headline PPI printed 0.3% m/m on Friday, against 0.8% previously and 0.4% expected.

This week's events: Nvidia Q3 earnings and Home Depot earnings Tuesday, Anthropic IPO with trading expected Wednesday 18 November (the text also says Thursday), FOMC minutes Wednesday, US retail sales Tuesday, UK and eurozone inflation data, and a slated Trump meeting with Xi Jinping and Putin on Thursday.

The desk's Exposure Optimisation Model cut global equity exposure to a neutral 43% from a bullish 70%, with every regional score revised lower. US equities fell to 40% from 70%. Europe fell to 73% from 90% but stays strong.

Technical View: US equities reversed sharply after the midterm elections as volatility rose across risk assets. Early signs of a rebound have appeared, but technical pressure may persist while key indices stay below important technical levels.

Sentiment and positioning: the post-midterm sell-off hit former tech leaders hardest while broader-market deterioration is comparatively contained. Risk appetite has reset and the defensive rotation is stretched. The S&P 500 is approaching key technical support. A durable low still needs confirmation.

The Nasdaq fell almost 15% below its peak, far more than the S&P 500. The desk sees no transmission from tech weakness to the broader market yet: economic momentum is resilient, forward S&P 500 EPS keeps rising and earnings revisions are positive. Options markets show risk has been materially repriced.

Q3 earnings season is solid for US corporates, with strong earnings growth, elevated beat rates and improving guidance. Revenue growth suggests the gains rest on resilient demand and not only on cost control. The desk screened the S&P 500 for 'Quadruple Winners', meaning companies with positive EPS and sales surprises that also raised full-year EPS and sales guidance.

sector_views.rationale: The post-midterm sell-off hit tech hardest, which the desk calls a meaningful reset in former leadership and not a broad breakdown. A durable low still needs confirmation.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports Q3 earnings Tuesday 17 November and Home Depot reports the same day. The report names them the big sector bellwethers for the week and gives no estimates.
US Q3 season: earnings growth still strong, beat rates elevated, guidance improving, with revenue growth supporting the earnings gains (desk summary, no figures given).

macro_indicators.interpretation: A hotter-than-expected print that triggered a Treasury sell-off and pushed Fed pricing toward a December hike.
Waller said a 50 bp December hike could be warranted if October core CPI remained at or above 0.3% m/m.
Came in below expectations, a softer producer-price reading than the CPI.
Yields rebounded on the CPI print and Waller's remarks.
Market pricing implies near certainty of a hike, with 55 bp of cumulative hikes through year-end 2027.
Crude fell on hopes of a US-Iran breakthrough, which supported European equities.

risk_factors: Hawkish Fed repricing: a December hike is near certain, and Waller floated 50 bp if October core CPI stays at or above 0.3% m/m.
Technical pressure may persist while key US indices stay below important technical levels.
A durable low in the tech sell-off still requires confirmation.
Contagion risk: tech weakness could spread if macro momentum and earnings revisions deteriorate. The desk sees no sign of that yet.
Event risk this week: Nvidia earnings, the Anthropic IPO and FOMC minutes.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility rose across risk assets after the midterm elections.
Sentiment and options markets show risk has been materially repriced. Risk appetite has reset and the defensive rotation is stretched.
The Exposure Optimisation Model cut global equity exposure to a neutral 43% from 70%, with US at 40% and Europe at 73%.
geopolitical: Hopes of a US-Iran breakthrough pushed crude lower, back toward USD 90-91 a barrel.
A Donald Trump meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin is slated for Thursday and will be watched closely.
Reported China spy allegations against Nvidia CEO Huang, who resigned, drove Nvidia headlines.
